evidence.ai_role: Learned structural predictions supply residue-level interface features for a specific analysis of observed genetic phenotypes.
evidence.tested: Existing FlyBase phenotype-associated missense variants mapped to predicted interfaces; within-gene permutation and conservation-adjusted association analyses.
evidence.unknown: Ascertainment bias and structural-model error remain; no new interaction-specific assay or causal phenotype test is represented. Novemberv5 higher-order assembly claims were not authenticated by this v1 review.

source_review.scope: Official v1 full Methods/Results: AFM interface definitions, 2,761 alleles/995 genes, permutation/conservation tests and structural limitations; official version history.

summary: FlyPredictome used AlphaFold-Multimer structures to test where previously reported Drosophila missense alleles occur. Across 2,761 mapped mutations in 995 genes, the highest predicted interaction-domain frequency bin had a 6.3-fold higher mutation rate than residues outside such domains; within-domain contact frequency added a 2.1-fold enrichment. Within-gene permutations and conservation adjustment supported a residue-level association. This retrospective structural–genetic association does not confirm every predicted interaction or establish causality. The represented result was public in the April 16 preprint; a November 23 version update surfaced it during this run.
title: Predicted fly protein interfaces are enriched for phenotype-associated mutations
